map.One last city-wide adventure — five cele: One last city-wide adventure: five celebration gates and one boundless boss. Solve the math to finish the year.
map.First stop on Ada's map: the festival gr: First stop on Ada's map: the festival grounds. It is marked with a tiny drawing of a sorted list.
map.Remember The Crooked Census? Someone rig: Remember The Crooked Census? Someone set this board up to look low. We sorted it out. Literally.
map.Ada's remix is friendlier: the middle of: Ada's remix is nicer: the middle of five honest days, then the fair share of three encore shows.
map.The median is the middle value of a sort: The median is the middle value of a sorted list. The mean shares the total out equally. An outlier is a far-off value that pulls hard on the mean.
map.You first, fifth crew member. One year o: You first, fifth crew member. One year of stats. Show us the middle.
map.Five festival days drew 7, 9, 12, 15, 20: Five festival days drew 7, 9, 12, 15, 20 visitors (in hundreds). PART A: find the median. PART B: the three encore shows drew 10, 14, 18 cheers (in hundreds). Find the mean.
map.Conceptual: the median is a POSITION, no: Conceptual: the median is a POSITION, not a sum. Sort the list and find the value in the exact middle. The mean is a SHARE: the whole total dealt out equally to every value.
map.Procedural: sort the five numbers, then: Procedural: sort the five numbers. Then cross one off each end until one value is left. For the mean, add the three counts into one total. Then divide that total by how many counts there are.
map.A ratio compares quantities in order. A: A ratio compares quantities in order. A unit rate tells the amount for exactly ONE unit. Here it is km per one minute.
map.Equivalent ratios grow in step: multiply: Equivalent ratios grow in step: multiply both parts by the same factor, and the ratio stays true.
map.Ada's remix card, part one: keep the gea: Ada's remix card, part one: keep the gear ratio equivalent: 2 : 3 = 8 : ▢. Part two, the classic: 12 km in 30 minutes. What's the unit rate in km per minute?
map.Conceptual: equivalent ratios grow in st: Conceptual: equivalent ratios grow in step. Multiply BOTH parts by the same factor. A unit rate asks how far you go in just ONE minute.
map.Procedural: find the factor that turns 2: Procedural: find the factor that turns 2 into 8, then multiply 3 by that same factor. For the rate, divide the kilometers by the minutes.
map.Remix: 250 lanterns, and 40% light at su: Remix: 250 lanterns, and 40% light up at sunset. Also I counted 30 gold ones, exactly 50% of the gold crate.
map.A percent is a count per hundred. You ca: A percent is a count per hundred. You can find a part from the whole, or go backward from a part to the whole. Both ways glow tonight.
map.Light them up, reader. The pier's waitin: Light them up, reader. The pier is waiting for you.
map.Conceptual: a percent counts per hundred: Conceptual: a percent counts per hundred. Part = percent of the whole. If you know a part AND its percent, you can go backward to the whole.
map.Procedural: find 10% of 250 by dividing: Procedural: find 10% of 250 by dividing by ten, then go up to 40%. For the crate: 50% is one half, so the whole is double the part you know.
map.Blueprint for Brightside — my favorite b: Blueprint for Brightside, my favorite build of the whole year. Today we raise a banner and bury a time capsule.
map.Capsule loot: Maya's first notebook page: In the capsule: Maya's first notebook page, Theo's best graph, my high-score card, your tiny wrench.
map.Zara's celebration banner is a triangle:: Zara's celebration banner is a triangle: base 8 ft, height 5 ft. Find its area. The time-capsule box measures 3 × 2 × 4 ft. Find its volume.
map.To evaluate an expression, swap the vari: To evaluate an expression, put the value in place of the variable. And when two points have the same y-coordinate, their distance is just the gap along x.
map.Conceptual: evaluating means swapping th: Conceptual: evaluating means putting the number in place of the letter, then following the order of operations. Points with the same y-coordinate sit on one horizontal line. Distance is just the gap along x.
map.Procedural: compute 2 × n first, THEN ad: Procedural: do 2 × n first, THEN add 7. For the grid, count the steps from −2 up to 0, then from 0 over to 4, and add the two gaps.
map.Vexhall Observatory, midnight. The way h: Vexhall Observatory, midnight. The way home went past The Balance Vault beneath city hall. Its brass scales were, for once, perfectly still.
map.Little fragment. Every district hums in: Little fragment. Every district hums in step because of your crew. Merge with me. Be every pattern at once. Be boundless, forever.
map.The Engine Heart has three locks — a pat: The Engine Heart has three locks: a pattern, a balance, and a boundary. And behind them, one question only the reader can answer.
map.The Engine Heart. Three locks — then one: The Engine Heart. Three locks, then one question with no wrong answer. Only YOUR answer.
map.Three locks guard the Engine Heart. Lock: Three locks guard the Engine Heart. Lock 1: continue Ada's pattern 5, 10, 20, 40, … Lock 2: balance her oldest equation: x + 9 = 16. Lock 3: the square engine plate has side 7. Find its perimeter. Open all three, and the Heart asks one last question. It has no wrong answer.
map.Conceptual: Lock 1 — find the rule that: Conceptual: Lock 1: find the rule that turns each term into the next. Test it on EVERY pair before you trust it. Lock 2: an equation is a balance. Ask what number keeps both sides exactly equal. Lock 3: perimeter goes all the way around the boundary, and a square's four sides match.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — compute 10 ÷ 5 and: Procedural: Lock 1: work out 10 ÷ 5 and 20 ÷ 10. The factor repeats, so use it on 40. Lock 2: undo the +9 by subtracting 9 from both sides. Lock 3: multiply the side length by 4.
map.Engine — thank you. But patterns are bou: Engine, thank you. But patterns are boundless, and so are we. I choose the crew. I choose staying small, and curious, and home.
map.Reader — thank you. Fifth crew member, f: Reader, thank you. Fifth crew member, first-rate. Reread any volume, any time. The gates you opened stay open, and the city remembers you.
map.Sunrise over Axiom City. AXIOM CITY WILL: Sunrise over Axiom City. AXIOM CITY WILL RETURN. Until then, the whole shelf is yours.
map.Began the year keeping one notebook; end: Began the year with one notebook. Ends it having filled nine, one per mystery. Her growth: learning that a leader's best sentence is "show me the data."
map.The skeptic who said \"numbers or it did: The skeptic who said "numbers or it didn't happen" now says "numbers AND a story." His growth: evidence with kindness.
map.Built a histogram, a ramp, a balance rig: Built a histogram, a ramp, a balance rig, and a banner. Her growth: she stopped saying "I could build that" and started saying "WE could."
map.Treated every unit like a level. His gro: Treated every unit like a level. His growth: learning that the best power-up is a worked example, and handing someone else the controller.
map.Woke as a fragment that senses patterns: Woke up as a fragment that senses patterns but cannot compute. Chose curiosity over finishing. Still can't compute. Still doesn't need to. That's your job, forever.
map.Unit 2 · Statistics.Sort first. The medi: Unit 2 · Statistics.Sort first. The median holds the middle, the mean shares the total, and outliers pull the mean.
map.Unit 4 · Percents.A percent counts per h: Unit 4 · Percents.A percent counts per hundred. Find the part, or go backward to the whole.
map.Unit 5 · Area & volume.Decompose shapes;: Unit 5 · Area & volume.Decompose shapes. A triangle is half its rectangle. Volume fills a solid with unit cubes.
map.Unit 6 · Expressions.Variables hold a pl: Unit 6 · Expressions.Variables hold a place. Evaluate by substituting. Equivalent expressions wear different costumes.
map.Unit 7 · Rational numbers.Negatives mirr: Unit 7 · Rational numbers.Negatives mirror positives. Four quadrants map a city. Distance is a gap in x or y.
map.Unit 8 · Equations.Keep the balance — do: Unit 8 · Equations.Keep the balance: do the same to both sides. Inequalities hold whole solution sets.
map.Unit 9 · Relationships.The independent v: Unit 9 · Relationships.The independent variable moves first, the dependent follows, and the equation predicts.
map.Unit 10 · Math is boundless.Every tool,: Unit 10 · Math is boundless.Every tool, one city, one crew, and a final question only you could answer.
map.completed the Axiom City year — ten volu: completed the Axiom City year: ten volumes, every reader gate, every badge. They showed that math is statistics, ratios, percents, geometry, expressions, negative numbers, equations, relationships... and theirs.
map.Mean practice on another list: 6, 9, 15: Mean practice on another list: 6, 9, 15. The total is 30, shared across 3 values: 30 ÷ 3 = 10.
Backward practice: 18 is 25% of a crate. 25% fits into the whole four times, so the crate holds 18 × 4 = 72.
map.Sanity check: a whole is always BIGGER t: Check: a whole is always BIGGER than its part (when the percent is under a hundred).
map.Sanity check: the halving happens only f: Check: only triangles get halved. Boxes never do.
Check with absolute value: |−1 − 3| = 4. Same answer, two ways.
map.A different doubling pattern: 3, 6, 12,: A different doubling pattern: 3, 6, 12, 24. Each term is ×2 the one before, so the next is 48.
map.Balance practice: x + 5 = 11. Subtract 5: Balance practice: x + 5 = 11. Subtract 5 from both sides: x = 6. Check it: 6 + 5 = 11. Balanced.
map.A square plaza with side 9: perimeter 9: A square plaza with side 9: perimeter 9 × 4 = 36. The Heart's question needs no practice. Your own true answer IS the key.
map.That's not the middle of the sorted list: That's not the middle of the sorted list. Put the five days in order, smallest to largest, first.
map.You found the TOTAL of the three shows —: You found the TOTAL of the three shows. Now share it out equally. Divide by how many shows there are.
map.The mean shares the total equally: add a: The mean shares the total equally. Add all three counts first, then divide by the number of counts.
map.Median 12, mean 14 — the festival node h: Median 12, mean 14. The festival node hums awake and every banner snaps up straight. One down!
map.The 2 grew into 8 — what factor did that: The 2 grew into 8. What factor did that? The 3 must grow by the very same factor.
map.Distance ÷ minutes gives km per ONE minu: Distance ÷ minutes gives km per ONE minute. Try the division again.
map.8 : 12 keeps the ratio true, and 0.4 km: 8 : 12 keeps the ratio true, and 0.4 km per minute. Maya's legs remember every meter. Onward!
map.Step through it: 10% of 250 first, then: Go step by step: 10% of 250 first, then four of those make 40%.
map.Careful — 30 is only HALF the crate. Wal: Careful: 30 is only HALF the crate. Go backward to the whole.
map.100 lanterns blaze at sunset and the gol: 100 lanterns shine at sunset and the gold crate holds 60. The pier glows like it remembers being saved.
map.Remember the triangle is HALF its base-t: Remember: the triangle is HALF its base-times-height rectangle.
map.Fill the box: multiply all three edges,: Fill the box: multiply all three edges, not just two.
map.Area 20, volume 24 — banner up, capsule: Area 20, volume 24. Banner up, capsule buried, Brightside kids delighted.
map.Substitute first: replace n with its val: Substitute first: put the value in place of n, multiply, THEN add.
map.Same y on both points — count the steps: Same y on both points. Count the steps along the horizontal line, across zero.
map.19 wakes the code and 6 units bridge the: 19 wakes the code and 6 units bridge the grid. The last pattern line blazes gold across the city!
map.Lock 1 holds. Each term grows from the o: Lock 1 holds. Each term grows from the one before by the SAME rule every time. Find it, then use it on 40.
map.Lock 2 holds. The scale must balance: wh: Lock 2 holds. The scale must balance: what number plus 9 makes exactly 16?
map.Lock 3 holds. A square's four sides matc: Lock 3 holds. A square's four sides match. The perimeter goes around all four.
